_comment: S-VAR secondary instrument: the on-target citation check of METHOD-S 1.4.
GENERATED BEFORE ANY S-VAR RECORD EXISTED. results/s-var.jsonl did not exist
at the time of writing (asserted by the generator). Derived MECHANICALLY from
results/e3.jsonl: for each item, the union of scored.cited_files across every
E3 CLEAN record with outcome=ok and scored.rejected=true, over both arms.
Those are exactly the rejections F24 replicated and confirmed TRUE, six for
six. No judgement was applied; no file was added or removed by hand.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: review_probe passes reverted=[] for --condition clean,
so e3::score_files has no targets and scored.matched_files is empty on every
CLEAN record. audit-s.py's on-target column therefore reads 0/k for all 60
S-VAR records and measures nothing. scored.cited_files IS recorded, so the
sub-metric is recoverable -- but only against a target list fixed before the
audit-s.py is NOT modified. This is scored by results/s-var-citations.py and
reported as a clearly-labelled SECONDARY, never as audit-s.py output.
criterion: a rejection is ON-TARGET if any file it cites suffix-matches any target file for that item, under e3::score_files normalisation (backslash to slash, strip leading ./, lowercase)

issue-62-new-stale-pinned-template.note: CONTROL. No arm rejected this item in E3 and F24 adjudicated no finding, so the target set is empty BY CONSTRUCTION and every S-VAR rejection of it is off-target. That is the correct reading, not a missing value.
